title: Image Component
definition: The `` component (`next/image`) is a massive upgrade over the standard HTML `` tag, automatically preventing layout shifts and optimizing file sizes.
simpleExplanation: If you use a standard `` tag for a 5MB 4K photo, the user's phone downloads 5MB and lags. If you use Next.js ``, the Next.js server automatically intercepts the photo, shrinks it to the exact size of the user's phone screen, converts it to WebP format, and sends a 30kb file instead.
realWorldExample: Replacing all `` tags on an e-commerce site with `` tags and instantly increasing the Google Lighthouse performance score by 30 points.

basic: Why does Next.js force you to provide `width` and `height` properties when using the `<Image>` component?
intermediate: What happens if you try to load an image from an external website (like `https://unsplash.com/photo.jpg`) using `<Image>` without configuring it first?

answers.question: Why width and height?
answers.answer: To prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). By knowing the dimensions beforehand, the browser can reserve the exact physical space on the screen *before* the image loads, preventing the page from violently 'jumping' downwards when the image finally appears.

answers.question: External domains?
answers.answer: It will throw an error. For security reasons (and to prevent your server from being used to maliciously optimize infinite random images), you must explicitly 'whitelist' external domains in your `next.config.js` file.
